question.:question/problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. The set $\{\mathbf{a}_{1}, \mathbf{a}_{2}, \mathbf{a}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent.

II. $-\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}+2\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$.

III. $x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$ only if $x_{1}=x_{2}=x_{3}=0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A set is **linearly independent** when the equation $x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$ has only the solution $x_{1}=x_{2}=x_{3}=0$. A nontrivial solution proves **linear dependence**.

Test the proposed combination:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}+2\mathbf{a}_{3}&=-\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+2\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}=\mathbf{0}\end{aligned}
$$

The homogeneous vector equation gives the coordinate system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}0 &=0 \\ x_{1}+x_{2} &=0 \\ 2x_{2}-x_{3} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Choose one coefficient nonzero and solve the remaining coordinate equations by substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x_{2}&=1 \\ x_{1}+(1)&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{1}=-1 \\ 2(1)-x_{3}&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{3}=2\end{aligned}
$$

This gives a nontrivial solution. Verify it directly:

$$
-\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}+2\mathbf{a}_{3}=-\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+2\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}=\mathbf{0}
$$

The coefficients are not all zero, so the set is **linearly dependent**.

Statement I is **false**. Statement II is **true**. Statement III is **false**.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$ only if $x_{1}=x_{2}=x_{3}=0$.

II. The set $\{\mathbf{a}_{1}, \mathbf{a}_{2}, \mathbf{a}_{3}\}$ is linearly dependent.

III. $-4\mathbf{a}_{1}-4\mathbf{a}_{2}+2\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A set is **linearly independent** when the equation $x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$ has only the solution $x_{1}=x_{2}=x_{3}=0$. A nontrivial solution proves **linear dependence**.

Test the proposed combination:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4\mathbf{a}_{1}-4\mathbf{a}_{2}+2\mathbf{a}_{3}&=-4\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}-4\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+2\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\ne\mathbf{0}\end{aligned}
$$

The homogeneous vector equation gives the coordinate system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1}-x_{3} &=0 \\ -x_{2}+x_{3} &=0 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Choose one coefficient nonzero and solve the remaining coordinate equations by substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x_{3}&=1 \\ x_{1}-(1)&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{1}=1 \\ -x_{2}+(1)&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives a nontrivial solution. Verify it directly:

$$
\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}+\mathbf{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}=\mathbf{0}
$$

The coefficients are not all zero, so the set is **linearly dependent**.

A failed candidate alone does not prove independence; the homogeneous-equation argument settles the classification.

Statement I is **false**. Statement II is **true**. Statement III is **false**.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$ only if $x_{1}=x_{2}=x_{3}=0$.

II. $-2\mathbf{a}_{1}+2\mathbf{a}_{2}+2\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$.

III. The set $\{\mathbf{a}_{1}, \mathbf{a}_{2}, \mathbf{a}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A set is **linearly independent** when the equation $x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$ has only the solution $x_{1}=x_{2}=x_{3}=0$. A nontrivial solution proves **linear dependence**.

Test the proposed combination:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2\mathbf{a}_{1}+2\mathbf{a}_{2}+2\mathbf{a}_{3}&=-2\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+2\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+2\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -2 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -2 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}\ne\mathbf{0}\end{aligned}
$$

The homogeneous vector equation gives the coordinate system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1}+x_{3} &=0 \\ x_{1} &=0 \\ 2x_{1}-x_{2} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Read a coordinate with just one remaining unknown at each step:

$$
\begin{aligned}x_{1}&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{1}=0 \\ (0)+x_{3}&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{3}=0 \\ 2(0)-x_{2}&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

Every coefficient must be zero. Thus the homogeneous equation has only the trivial solution and the set is **linearly independent**.

A failed candidate alone does not prove independence; the homogeneous-equation argument settles the classification.

Statement I is **true**. Statement II is **false**. Statement III is **true**.
